newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain sees no near-term revision in '97 GDP target.
newsitem.headline: Spain sees no near-term revision in '97 GDP target.

text.p: Spain does not intend to upwardly revise its 1997 gross domestic product target in the short-term, Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said on Wednesday.

"The government will not revise (the GDP target) in the short run. Before this revision takes place, we need confirmation of the strengthening of the economy," Montoro told reporters at a seminar in Madrid.
The government's 1997 GDP target stands at 3.0 percent. After recent economic data showed a pickup in the economy, some analysts forecast growth at 3.2 or 3.3 percent.
Montoro said the acceleration in growth was boosting employment and helping to meet budget targets.
He was also optimistic on the inflation outlook.
He said a pickup in inflation in June was "not necessarily" expected. May inflation was up 1.5 percent year-on-year.
Spain will easily meet its downwardly revised CPI target of 2.2 percent for this year, Montoro said.
